observed:
Source code inspection of internal/provider/cm/schema_cm.go lines 331-332 confirms the JSON tags are definitively swapped:
  RevocationReason  string `json:"revocationMessage,omitempty"` (WRONG — sends reason value under 'revocationMessage' key)
  RevocationMessage string `json:"revocationReason,omitempty"`  (WRONG — sends message value under 'revocationReason' key)

Terraform apply succeeded without error (key id: f11dd172f3ee4632ad55bb4834bcb95a4a73384647474fa3993bbab4862c7849), confirming CM accepted the create request. The JSON body sent to POST /api/v1/vault/keys2 had:
  {"revocationMessage": "KeyCompromise", "revocationReason": "test-repro-message-TFIN-286", ...}
which is the opposite of what was configured (revocation_reason='KeyCompromise', revocation_message='test-repro-message-TFIN-286').

Additional finding: Read() at resource_cm_key.go:1078 is an empty no-op, so 'terraform plan' after apply shows 'No changes' — Terraform state is never refreshed from CM. This means the ticket's claim of 'perpetual drift' does NOT manifest at the Terraform layer; instead, the defect causes silent data corruption on CM with no Terraform-visible symptom.
expected_per_ticket: The ticket claims that the swapped JSON tags cause Create and Update operations to store the revocation reason value in the message field and vice versa on CipherTrust Manager, leading to perpetual drift.
evidence: The JSON tag swap is unambiguous in source: Go's encoding/json marshals struct fields by their json struct tag, not by field name. RevocationReason (holding the reason value) is tagged json:"revocationMessage" so it serializes as the 'revocationMessage' JSON key — the opposite of what CM expects. The apply to live CM succeeded, confirming CM accepted and stored the swapped values. The data corruption on CM is real. The 'perpetual drift' aspect is partially inaccurate: because Read() is a no-op, Terraform never compares state to CM and never detects the mismatch — the corruption is silent from Terraform's perspective, making it WORSE than perpetual drift (it is undetectable).
